rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent dominant mass in all four views, with a clear bent-bar gesture and acceptable continuity across view transitions. It is not coherent in only one view, and the solids do not visibly collide. The parcel response is decent: the form sits inside the green boundary and maintains a dominant orientation rather than merely filling the box. However, the blue frontage edge is not strongly answered; the mass feels too sealed at the ground and the open-space figure is weak, so publicness is limited. Programmatically it can plausibly support neighborhood living/commercial mixed-use because it has a compact capacity-aware volume and some upper articulation, but the section logic does not yet convincingly express an active ground threshold plus terrace/court relation. The silhouette is mildly stepped/tapered but not enough to count as a strong inhabited section; it is more a compact sculpted prism than a robust public-section building.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much taller and more tower-like than this neighborhood-living brief; transfer only the mass continuity and stepped/crowned profile, not the typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact prism can gain identity through a controlled taper and a clear upper articulation while remaining a legible single mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office tower typology and extreme height are not directly relevant to this low-rise neighborhood program.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A subtle vertical skew and continuous envelope can preserve one dominant mass while introducing directional tension.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a low pavilion, so the scale and roof logic should not be copied; only the active-edge/entry-seam principle transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A small commercial mass can still read as neighborhood-active when the ground edge is opened and a public threshold is made explicit.
